lane: Gamification, progression, leaderboards, accounts, and the dark-pattern audit
headline: Re-plan the Floodlight bible around one identity hook (the club/team/driver you support), one currency (ad-earned coins, never purchasable), sport-calendar seasons, and bracketed/club/friends leaderboards that show percentile not rank below the top; make the rewarded ad a priced, capped, post-match choice with a visible free alternative; and hard-ban the eleven patterns the FTC, EU CPC/UCPD/DSA and India DPDP/Gaming Act are now enforcing against this exact genre.

findings.finding: WHAT ALREADY EXISTS AND MUST BE RE-PLANNED, NOT REBUILT. The repo's design bible (/home/user/fact-duel/public/product/gamification/design-bible.md) has: XP curve xpToNext(l)=round(80*l^1.55) with titles Rookie->Legend; day-streaks with shields (max 2, earned every 7 days); 3 seeded daily quests; combos x1.25..x2; speed bonus; device-local Arena Rank Bronze->Diamond; ~30 achievements; gems + Locker cosmetics; honest near-miss margin; 'on this device' labels. The in-progress economy (/home/user/fact-duel/lib/economy/economy.mjs DEFAULT_CONFIG) already encodes: adReward by region {US:50, GB:45, DE:40, FR:40, IN:20, '*':30}, adDailyCap 20, adCooldownMs 45000, daily grant 30, practiceEntry 10, stakes [10,25,50,100,250], floor 25 coins every 6h, softCap 5000, and four ad placements ['coins','practice-entry','duel-entry','continue'] (/home/user/fact-duel/lib/ads/provider.mjs). The economy header itself forbids loss-streak mercy rigging. The compliance research (/home/user/fact-duel/public/product/compliance/compliance.json) has already verified the FTC Epic/Cognosphere benchmarks, the CPC Key Principles (21 Mar 2025) and the India Act (in force 1 May 2026). Everything below builds on those artefacts.
findings.evidence: design-bible.md sections 3-4 and 9; economy.mjs lines 30-58; provider.mjs PLACEMENTS; compliance.json regions[0].checklist[9], regions[1].checklist[17,38-42], regions[2].posture.

findings.finding: (1) ACCOUNT & PROFILE DESIGN. Identity hook = sport-fan allegiance, because supporters already carry a public identity they want to display (Cialdini et al. 1976, 'Basking in Reflected Glory: Three (Football) Field Studies', 2,369 citations: fans wear team colours after wins and say 'we won' / 'they lost'; Cialdini, Influence, Ch. 'Liking'/'Unity' and Pre-Suasion Part 3 'unity of we'). PROFILE = a 'Supporter Card': (a) handle + avatar; (b) up to one allegiance per sport: club (football), franchise/national side (cricket), team (MLB/NBA), driver AND constructor (F1); (c) per-sport rating and rank tier, per-sport 'caps' (matches played, in the sport's own vocabulary), best sport; (d) season medals for the current real season; (e) current matchweek streak; (f) rivals list (people you have dueled 3+ times) and head-to-head record; (g) Vault count. WHY PEOPLE FILL IT IN: each field unlocks something the player wants in Hooked terms (Eyal, Ch. 5 'Investment' - stored value that loads the next trigger): choosing a club = joins that club's board and derby weeks; choosing a driver = race-weekend triple duel; adding rivals = rematch trigger. Endowed progress (Nunes & Dreze 2006, 'The Endowed Progress Effect', J. Consumer Research): the card starts 2/7 complete after the first duel (handle + first sport auto-filled). GUEST-FIRST: never gate first play behind account creation - Baymard's US shopper survey lists 'The site wanted me to create an account' as an 18% abandonment reason; the account is offered at the first moment stored value exists (first win, first rank promotion, first club board) using Hooked's investment logic. Server principal is minted anonymously and promoted in place (compliance roadmap M4), so a guest's record is never lost on sign-up. AUTH: email magic link + Google + Apple; if any third-party social login is used, Apple guideline 4.8 requires an equivalent privacy-preserving option (relevant if the web app is ever wrapped). MINORS: default to no allegiance-based ad targeting; India DPDP treats under-18 as children and bars tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising directed at children (PRS/Wikipedia summaries; penalty up to Rs 200 crore for children's obligations); EU DSA Art 28(2) bars profiling-based ads to minors; US COPPA 2025 amendments require separate verifiable parental consent for disclosures for targeted advertising. Therefore the profile carries an age band captured at sign-up and the ad seam requests contextual (non-profiled) rewarded ads for any unverified-age or under-18 account in all three markets.
findings.evidence: Semantic Scholar record for DOI 10.1037/0022-3514.34.3.366 (Cialdini 1976); Baymard cart-abandonment list; PRS India DPDP brief; EUR-Lex DSA Art 28(2); FTC COPPA press release 16 Jan 2025; Apple App Review Guideline 4.8; compliance roadmap M4 (/home/user/fact-duel/public/product/compliance/roadmap.md).

findings.finding: (2) PROGRESSION RE-PLAN. WHAT REPLACES GEMS: nothing purchasable and nothing stakeable. Gems are deleted as a currency; the product runs ONE currency (coins: earned by ads, daily grant, duel wins, floor; spent on stakes and drill entries). Cosmetics (frames, club kits, driver liveries, titles) move to ACHIEVEMENT and SEASON unlocks, never to a second currency. Rationale: two-tier currencies are exactly what the FTC targeted in Cognosphere (order requires disclosure of 'exchange rates for multi-tiered virtual currency') and what deceptive.design catalogues as 'Currency Confusion'; and the CPC Key Principles footnote 2 excludes 'in-game currencies obtainable solely through gameplay and not purchasable with real-world money' - keeping coins non-purchasable keeps the whole virtual-currency principle set off the product (compliance.json risks[39]). SPORT-SPECIFIC RANKS (per-sport rating, Glicko/Elo-style, skill not grind - Schell's 'Lens of Fairness' and 'Lens of Skill'; Pink, Drive Part 2 'Mastery' - progress must track competence not hours): Football: Sunday League -> Non-League -> Fourth Tier -> Second Tier -> Top Flight -> Continental -> Ballon (generic names; do not use 'Premier League' or club trademarks inside rank names - IP clearance UNVERIFIED, counsel item). Cricket: Gully -> Club -> Domestic -> First-Class -> International Cap -> Hundred Club. Baseball: Rookie Ball -> Single-A -> Double-A -> Triple-A -> Majors -> Cooperstown. F1: Karting -> F4 -> F3 -> F2 -> Race Seat -> Podium -> World Champion. Basketball: Rec League -> Varsity -> College -> Development League -> Pro -> All-Star -> Hall of Fame. Tiers have promotion ceremonies (existing) and demotion floors once reached (existing Arena Rank rule) - Octalysis Core Drive 2 (Accomplishment) with a Core Drive 8 (Loss & Avoidance) floor so relegation cannot wipe a season. ACCOUNT-WIDE LEVEL/XP stays as tenure (titles Rookie->Legend) but is de-emphasised on comparative surfaces. SEASONS ALIGNED TO REAL CALENDARS (verified dates): Football season = Premier League 21 Aug 2026 - 30 May 2027 (Champions League league phase 8-10 Sep 2026, final 5 Jun 2027, Madrid); Basketball season = NBA 20 Oct 2026 - 11 Apr 2027 with an NBA Cup mini-season 30 Oct - 11 Dec 2026, All-Star 21 Feb 2027, play-in 13-16 Apr 2027; F1 season = 14 Mar - 12 Dec 2027, 24 rounds (each Grand Prix weekend is a 'round' with its own mini-board); Baseball season = MLB Opening Day 25 Mar 2027 (standalone game 24 Mar), regular season ends 26 Sep, All-Star 13 Jul, World Series 22-30 Oct 2027 - with a lockout risk because the CBA expires 1 Dec 2026, so the baseball season must be able to run as an 'Off-season / Hot Stove' mode; Cricket = IPL window (2026 ran 28 Mar - 31 May; 2027 dates UNVERIFIED, page does not exist yet) plus ICC Cricket World Cup 4 Oct - 21 Nov 2027 (South Africa/Zimbabwe/Namibia, 14 teams). Each real season = one FACT//DUEL season: rating soft-resets (squash toward the tier floor, not to zero - Duolingo-style weekly leagues showed tripling of highly-engaged learners with periodic resets), season medal minted at close, off-season runs 'Transfer Window'/'Winter League'/'Hot Stove' story routes (McGonigal, Reality Is Broken Ch. 6 'epic scale' - a collective 'the community has mapped 61% of the 2026-27 season' meter). DAILY QUESTS become FIXTURE QUESTS seeded from the events calendar (/home/user/fact-duel/lib/events-data.mjs) rather than random topics. STREAK becomes a MATCHWEEK STREAK for football/cricket/NBA/MLB (one qualifying play per real matchweek/series) and a RACE-WEEKEND STREAK for F1; shields are kept (Duolingo: allowing up to two Freezes raised daily active learners +0.38%; 7-day streak reachers are 3.6x more likely to complete a course). Combos, speed bonus, honest margin and ceremonies are unchanged.
findings.evidence: FTC Cognosphere press release 17 Jan 2025; deceptive.design 'Currency Confusion'; compliance.json risks[39] (CPC footnote 2); Wikipedia season pages for 2026-27 Premier League, 2026-27 UEFA Champions League, 2026-27 NBA, 2027 F1, 2027 MLB, 2026 IPL, 2027 Cricket World Cup; Duolingo blog 31 Jan 2022; Lenny's Newsletter (Mazal, 28 Feb 2023).

findings.finding: (3) LEADERBOARDS THAT DO NOT DEMORALISE THE 95%. The evidence that global boards demotivate: Hanus & Fox 2015 (Computers & Education, 1,821 citations, 16-week longitudinal classroom study with a badges+leaderboard condition) found the gamified group reporting LOWER intrinsic motivation, satisfaction and empowerment over time and lower final exam scores mediated by motivation (abstract paywalled; finding stated from the paper, sample size not re-verified); Christy & Fox 2014 (Computers & Education, 258 citations, 'Leaderboards in a virtual classroom: a test of stereotype threat and social comparison explanations for women's math performance') found that the COMPOSITION of the leaderboard changed women's maths performance - the board's social comparison, not the score, did the damage; Landers, Bauer & Callan 2017 (Computers in Human Behavior) modelled leaderboards as goal-setting: a board works like a difficult goal, and when the top is unreachable it becomes an 'impossible goal' and performance effects vanish (abstract not fetched, finding from the paper); Bai, Hew & Huang 2020 meta-analysis (30 interventions, 3,202 participants, Hedges' g = 0.504 overall) notes the controversy ('exploitationware') and mixed evidence. Duolingo's own numbers show what works when bracketed: small weekly leagues raised learning time 17% and tripled highly engaged learners. DESIGN: (a) BRACKETS: leagues of 30 players formed by sport rating tier AND recent activity, weekly reset on the sport's natural boundary (Monday 00:00 local for football/cricket/NBA/MLB; Monday after the race for F1); top 10 promote; no relegation in a player's first two weeks (endowed progress, Nunes & Dreze) and never from the bottom tier. (b) FRIENDS board is the DEFAULT view once a player has 3+ friends (SDT relatedness; Ryan, Rigby & Przybylski 2006 PENS - relatedness independently predicts return play; research-brief rule 'small friend leagues 5-10 people rather than global boards'). (c) CLUB boards: 'Arsenal supporters this week' - the player competes FOR the club (BIRG, Cialdini 1976) and the club competes in a Derby Week board against its real rival (Schell, 'Lens of Competition' and 'Lens of Cooperation' - team competition converts losers into contributors). (d) NEIGHBOURHOOD WINDOW: every board renders the player with 2 above and 2 below plus the promotion line, never the full table first (goal-gradient: Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng 2006, 'The Goal-Gradient Hypothesis Resurrected', J. Marketing Research - effort accelerates as the goal nears; a distant #1 is an impossible goal per Landers). (e) PERCENTILE, NOT RANK, for global: 'Top 12% of cricket fans this week' - everyone outside the top 100 sees a percentile and their own delta ('+3 places'), which converts downward comparison into self-comparison (Kahneman, Thinking Fast and Slow Ch. 26-28: losses relative to a reference point loom larger, so choose the reference point = last week's self). (f) YOU-VS-YOU board: personal best per sport, the only board shown on a loss result screen. (g) HONESTY: no bots on any board, no fabricated presence, 'players who played this week' count is real, ties broken visibly, and a board that has fewer than 5 humans says so rather than padding (design-bible section 9). (h) A player can hide from boards (autonomy, Pink Drive Part 2; opt-in leagues per McGonigal's voluntary-participation trait). DSA NOTE: public leaderboards carrying user-authored handles are user content disseminated to the public - compliance.json risks[37] warns this can flip the service into a DSA 'online platform' (Arts 20-28); keep handles moderated and treat the board launch as a DSA scoping gate.
findings.evidence: Semantic Scholar/OpenAlex records for DOIs 10.1016/j.compedu.2014.08.019, 10.1016/j.compedu.2014.05.005; Semantic Scholar record for 10.1016/j.edurev.2020.100322; Lenny's Newsletter (Mazal 2023); research-brief SDT/PENS section; compliance.json risks[37].

findings.finding: (4) CORE LOOP REDESIGNED AROUND THE AD-FOR-COINS MOMENT ('a choice, not a toll'). Rules, each with its source: (a) THE AD IS PRICED AND LABELLED BEFORE THE TAP: 'Watch a 30s ad -> +50 coins' (region value from config), with the free alternatives on the same card: 'Daily 30 coins (claimed)', 'Floor: 25 coins in 2h 10m', 'Win a duel'. Google Play's Ads policy exempts only 'rewarded ads which are explicitly opted-in by users (for example, an ad that developers explicitly offer a user to watch in exchange for unlocking a specific game feature)'; AdMob defines rewarded ads as 'served after a user explicitly chooses to view'. (b) PLACEMENTS: keep 'coins' (wallet top-up at lobby/result) and 'practice-entry' (pay 10 coins OR watch); DELETE 'duel-entry' as an ad placement - an ad to enter a duel is a toll and reads as forced action (deceptive.design 'Forced action'); restrict 'continue' to practice drills only, never inside a live duel (review evidence SP02/QP01: ads inside timed play caused losses). (c) TIMING: ads only at natural breaks - after the result receipt is saved and shown (SP01 requirement: save the receipt BEFORE optional follow-on content), never between question readiness and answer lock (timing contract in the advisor skill). (d) RECIPROCITY FIRST: the daily grant and the floor arrive before any ad is offered (Cialdini, Influence Ch. 2 Reciprocity; Ariely, Predictably Irrational Ch. 3 'The Cost of Zero Cost' - FREE has outsized pull, so the free path must be real, not decorative). (e) 'NOW THAT' NOT 'IF-THEN': the ad reward is framed as a top-up you chose, never as a condition of finishing something you started (Pink, Drive Ch. 2 and 2A: contingent if-then rewards crowd out intrinsic motivation; unexpected now-that rewards do not). (f) VISIBLE CAP: 'Ad boosts today: 3 of N' with N shown; the current config cap of 20/day is a hypothesis to be tested, and the cap must be visible so it never reads as a hidden rule (SP03 complaint pattern). (g) VARIABLE REWARD LIVES IN PLAY, NOT IN THE AD: Wild Round multipliers stay on questions (Hooked Ch. 4 Rewards of the Hunt); the ad payout is FIXED and disclosed - a randomised ad reward would import the loot-box odds problem the FTC ordered Cognosphere to disclose. (h) STAKE CHOICE BEFORE THE LOBBY, from the legal stake ladder [10,25,50,100,250]; a player at the floor can always afford the 10 stake or one drill (economy.mjs floor) so nobody is ever locked out - that is the honest answer to 'energy/lives' mechanics. (i) NEVER let an ad buy competitive advantage inside a duel (no ad-bought extra time, 50/50 or second chance in ranked play) - QP05 complaint ('ad-funded retries unequal'), Schell's Lens of Fairness. (j) AD FAILURE IS NOT THE PLAYER'S FAULT: if the provider returns completed:false the UI must offer the other way in (provider.mjs NullAdProvider contract) and never charge the player time - TC03/SP01 'black ad screen' pattern. (k) LOOP MAP (Hooked): Trigger = fixture card / rival rematch / streak flame; Action = one tap into a duel; Variable reward = round outcome, combo, rating delta, fixture-quest tick; Investment = stake choice, club allegiance, rival list, Vault save; the ad sits OFF the loop as an optional wallet top-up shown only when coins < next stake. Benchmarks for rewarded-ad opt-in and retention lift could not be fetched from a primary source in this session and are UNVERIFIED; instrument them (Lean Analytics: One Metric That Matters for this stage = D7 retention of duel-completers, with ad opt-in rate and ads-per-DAU as guardrail metrics).
findings.evidence: Google Play Ads policy (support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9857753); AdMob 'Overview of rewarded ad units'; provider.mjs and economy.mjs; trivia-reviews.md SP01, SP02, SP03, QP01, QP05, TC03; FTC Cognosphere order terms.

findings.finding: (5) RETENTION LOOP TIED TO REAL FIXTURES. Daily/weekly external triggers (Hooked Ch. 2) that only exist because the sport calendar exists, all derived from the curated static events calendar (no live data is implied - events-calendar.md rule): (a) FIXTURE CARD on Home: 'Tonight: Arsenal v Spurs - play the North London derby duel' (Berger, Contagious 'Triggers': tie the product to something already in the environment); (b) RESULTS-MORNING RECAP: a 5-question 'Yesterday' drill the day after a matchday/race, entered with coins or free once per day; (c) MATCHWEEK STREAK and RACE-WEEKEND TRIPLE (practice Fri, qualifying Sat, race Sun) with shields and honest 'streak at stake' copy that always offers the shield (design-bible section 9); (d) SEASON MILESTONES: All-Star break, NBA Cup final, MLB Opening Day, IPL final, Champions League final as limited modes (already supported by MODE_TEMPLATES in /home/user/fact-duel/lib/events.mjs); (e) RIVAL RETURN: 'Your rival played the derby duel - rematch?' only when true and only with notification consent (QP06 complaint: score checks sending unconsented nudges); (f) PEAK-END: the result screen ends on the margin + one-tap rematch + Vault save (Kahneman Ch. 35-36 peak-end rule; Schell interest curve - climax at the final double-value question). Off-season retention uses story routes (Expeditions) rather than manufactured urgency (Octalysis: White Hat long loop, Black Hat only at the daily-return moment). Streak-anxiety guard: streak length copy shifts from growth framing early to loss framing late (Duolingo's stated design), but the app never sends 'streak dying' messages without a one-tap shield, and never charges coins to repair a streak (a coin sink on loss aversion is the Duolingo streak-repair pattern applied to an ad economy = paying attention to avoid loss, which the CPC reads as pressure).
findings.evidence: events-calendar.md; lib/events.mjs; Duolingo blog 31 Jan 2022; trivia-reviews.md QP06; design-bible sections 3 and 9.

findings.finding: (6) VIRALITY. Mechanics and their sources: (a) CHALLENGE LINK - async 'Settle it' duel by URL (StoryBrand: the character's problem is the unsettled argument; the app is the guide with a plan: pick sport -> send link -> loser buys the coffee); Berger STEPPS 'Social Currency' (proving you know more) and 'Public' (the result card is designed to be seen). (b) RESULT SHARE CARD: sport-coded card with margin, club crest colour (not trademark art - IP UNVERIFIED), and percentile; 'Emotion' (pride) and 'Stories' in STEPPS. (c) CLUB RIVALRY WEEKS: derby-week board totals are public and shareable ('Arsenal fans lead Spurs fans 1,204-988 this week') - BIRG and Cialdini Unity; McGonigal's 'vicarious pride' and 'happy embarrassment' as prosocial emotions (Reality Is Broken Ch. 5). (d) REFERRAL: both sides receive coins (no money, no prize) - permitted where HQ Trivia's referral-for-lives was, but capped, disclosed, and never worded as a direct exhortation to children (UCPD Annex I point 28 is blacklisted hard law). (e) FRIEND ROOMS already exist (Play screen); add 'invite a rival' from the rival list. (f) MEASURE (Traction, Weinberg & Mares Ch. on Viral Marketing; Lean Analytics Virality stage): viral coefficient K = invites per user x acceptance rate, and cycle time; K is unknown today and must be measured, not assumed. (g) NEVER fabricate social proof to seed virality ('12 friends are playing' when they are not) - deceptive.design 'Fake social proof'; Booking.com's 2019 CPC commitments are the enforcement precedent for activity messages.
findings.evidence: trivia-reviews.md QD01 (clubs requested), QuizDuel Teams help; Booking.com commitments press release 20 Dec 2019; EUR-Lex UCPD Annex I point 28; market.md wedges.

findings.finding: DARK-PATTERN CATALOGUE (what it exploits / retention effect / enforcement / verdict). Genre examples are from primary regulator texts or the repo's inspected reviews; where an example is from general knowledge it is marked likely. --- P1 NEAR-MISS (fabricated 'so close' outcomes). Exploits: reward-circuit recruitment - Clark, Lawrence, Astley-Jones & Gray 2009 (Neuron 61:481-490): near-misses were rated less pleasant yet 'increased desire to play', activating ventral striatum and anterior insula like real wins, only when the player had control (choice); Kahneman: counterfactual regret. Retention: short-term more sessions (the Clark effect); long-term it is the gambling mechanic - Belgium's Gaming Commission 2018 position and the CPC treat whales as a vulnerable group (compliance.json risks[26]). Enforcement: no dedicated statute, but a fabricated margin is a misleading practice under UCPD Art 6 and FTC Act s.5 (deception). Verdict: NEVER fabricate; USE the honest true-margin display already in the bible. --- P2 ARTIFICIAL SCARCITY / FALSE URGENCY (countdowns, 'only 2 left', limited-time bundles). Exploits: Cialdini Scarcity (Influence Ch. 7); Kahneman loss aversion; Ariely 'Keeping Doors Open' (Ch. 8). Retention: short spikes, long-term erosion of trust once timers are seen to repeat. Enforcement: UCPD Annex I point 7 blacklists 'falsely stating that a product will only be available for a very limited time'; FTC 2022 report 'Bringing Dark Patterns to Light' names 'countdown timers designed to make consumers believe they only have a limited time'; Booking.com committed in Dec 2019 to 'not present an offer as being time-limited if the same price will still be available afterwards'; the CPC action against Star Stable (21 Mar 2025) cites 'time-limited purchase pressure tactics'. Verdict: NEVER fake; USE real scarcity only - fixture windows are genuinely limited ('the derby duel closes at kick-off'), and that is the whole reason a sports calendar is an honest urgency engine. --- P3 STREAK-LOSS ANXIETY (streak repair purchases, alarmist notifications, no freeze). Exploits: loss aversion and the sunk-cost 'prison' (Octalysis Core Drive 8); Duolingo's own statement that longer streaks 'leverage loss aversion'. Retention: Duolingo evidence is that streaks help when there is a freeze (+0.38% DAU from two equipped freezes; 7-day reachers 3.6x more likely to complete) and the review corpus shows dislike of pressure (learning reviews L01-L04 in review-research.md). Enforcement: not a named offence; a coin/attention charge to repair a streak aimed at a minor audience is the 'pressure' the CPC principles and UCPD Art 8 (undue influence) describe. Verdict: USE streaks with matchweek granularity, free shields, honest copy; NEVER sell or ad-gate streak repair, never message 'streak dying' without the shield. --- P4 DISGUISED AD-CLOSE / UNCLOSABLE ADS (fake X, delayed X, ads mid-play, black screens that eat the round). Exploits: attention capture and mis-tap (Kahneman System 1 / WYSIATI). Retention: immediate churn - SP01 'unclosable ads and a black results screen', SP02 'ads now interrupting active quizzes', TC01 'ad-related freezing', TC03 'black ad screens', QP01 'round losses after setting the phone aside during an ad'. Enforcement: Google Play Ads policy bans 'a false dismiss button', interstitials 'not closeable after 15 seconds', and ads 'that show unexpectedly, typically when the user has chosen to do something else'; Coalition for Better Ads standards (150,000+ consumers researched) list pop-ups, prestitials, postitials with countdown and large sticky ads as beneath the standard for mobile web; FTC report category 'Misleading Consumers and Disguising Ads'. Verdict: NEVER; the rewarded format with provider-controlled close is the only ad surface. --- P5 CONFIRMSHAMING (guilt-worded decline buttons). Exploits: Cialdini Consistency (Influence Ch. 3) and social-norm framing (Ariely Ch. 4 'The Cost of Social Norms'); DSA Art 25(3) example 'non-neutral presentation of options'. Enforcement: Amazon Prime settlement 25 Sep 2025 - $2.5bn ($1bn civil penalty + $1.5bn refunds) over enrolment 'without their affirmative consent' and 'Misleading button language ("No, I don't want Free Shipping")'; Epic order bars 'counterintuitive button configurations'. Verdict: NEVER; decline copy is neutral ('Not now'), same size and contrast as accept. --- P6 FORCED CONTINUITY / HARD-TO-CANCEL / ENTITLEMENT REVOCATION. Exploits: inertia and default effects (Kahneman Ch. 27-28 endowment/status quo). Retention: QD04 'update replaced previously paid ad removal with renewed ads and subscription demands' - entitlement trust destroyed. Enforcement: ROSCA (15 U.S.C. 8401-8405) requires clear disclosure, express informed consent and simple cancellation; FTC's 2024 click-to-cancel rule was vacated (Custom Communications v. FTC, 8th Cir., 8 Jul 2025) but ROSCA and the Amazon order stand; FTC report example ABCmouse ('Easy Cancellation' hiding 'a difficult-to-find, lengthy, and confusing cancellation path'); DSA Art 25(3) 'making cancellation more burdensome than signup'; EU DCD Art 19 limits devaluing a paid digital service. Verdict: N/A for money (no purchases) but the SAME rule applies to coins: never silently change what coins buy (TC03) - publish coin-rule changes in advance in-app. --- P7 HIDDEN ODDS (loot boxes, mystery multipliers, undisclosed matchmaking). Exploits: probability neglect and overweighting of small chances (Kahneman Ch. 29-30). Enforcement: FTC v. Cognosphere, 17 Jan 2025, $20m: 'Misrepresenting loot box odds', 'obscuring real costs through confusing multi-tiered virtual currency', order requires odds and exchange-rate disclosure and a direct real-money purchase option, and bans loot-box sales to under-16s without parental consent; Apple guideline 3.1.1 requires odds disclosure for randomised purchases; compliance.json checklist[23] forbids chance in any paid path. Verdict: NEVER sell or ad-gate randomised rewards; USE Wild Round only if its frequency (~1 in 6) and multipliers are printed in the rules, and label bot opponents (a court entered a nine-figure judgment in July 2026 over real-money matches secretly filled with bots - compliance roadmap G4). --- P8 'ONE MORE' LOOPS (auto-queue, overlay reward chains, no stopping cue). Exploits: Zeigarnik and variable-ratio schedules (Hooked Ch. 4); Octalysis 'torture breaks' inverted. Retention: TC02 'reward/event prompts obstructing play' - the reviewer distinguishes prompt spam from ads. Enforcement: DSA Art 25(3) 'repeated requests for already-made decisions'; deceptive.design 'Nagging' and 'Addictive Design'; the forthcoming EU Digital Fairness Act (proposal slated Q3 2026 per Wikipedia; Q4 2026 per the repo's Legislative Train check - date contested) targets addictive design explicitly. Verdict: USE a single one-tap rematch and the 'Resume 3/7' Zeigarnik card; NEVER auto-start the next duel, never chain more than one reward overlay, always show an exit (McGonigal: voluntary participation). --- P9 SOCIAL-PROOF FABRICATION (fake opponents, fake 'X playing now', fake activity feeds, unconsented nudges). Exploits: Cialdini Social Proof (Ch. 4). Retention: QD01 believed opponents were real (no bot audit); QP06 score checks sent nudges the viewer did not intend. Enforcement: UCPD Annex I point 22 (falsely representing oneself as a consumer) and Art 6; Booking.com 2019 commitments on 'X people looking' style claims; FTC Act s.5; deceptive.design 'Fake social proof'. Verdict: NEVER; bots stay labelled, counts are real, profile views are read-only. --- P10 DRIP PRICING / HIDDEN COSTS (junk fees, currency bundles that never divide evenly). Exploits: anchoring and relativity (Ariely Ch. 1; Kahneman Ch. 11). Enforcement: FTC Junk Fees Rule (announced 17 Dec 2024, effective 12 May 2025) requires 'the true total price inclusive of all mandatory fees' up front; FTC report example LendingClub fees 'hid behind tooltip buttons'; CPC Principle 3 targets bundles that mismatch prices and denying the player a choice of amount. Verdict: NEVER; with no purchases the analogue is the stake and the drill entry - show the full coin cost and the post-stake balance before the commit tap. --- P11 (genre extra) CHILD-DIRECTED EXHORTATION and PROFILED ADS TO MINORS. Enforcement: UCPD Annex I point 28 (hard law, blacklisted); Star Stable CPC action (21 Mar 2025) for 'direct appeals to children'; DSA Art 28(2); India DPDP s.9 (no tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising directed at under-18s); COPPA 2025 amendments (separate consent for targeted-ad disclosures; compliance one year from Federal Register publication). Verdict: NEVER; contextual ads only for unverified/under-18, no 'ask your parents' copy, no allegiance targeting for minors.

findings.finding: USE LIST (persuasive, honest, defensible) with the honest implementation: U1 Real deadlines from the sport calendar (fixture windows, matchweek resets) - Cialdini Scarcity applied to a true constraint; copy states the real close time. U2 Streaks with free shields, matchweek granularity, growth-then-loss framing, never repairable for coins/ads. U3 Honest near-miss margin ('Lost by one round - Q3 was 0.9s slower') with one-tap rematch. U4 Endowed progress (card 2/7, league meter 2/10, 'Camp 1 reached'). U5 Goal-gradient (neighbourhood window, '2 wins to promote', ticks accelerate near the end). U6 Zeigarnik resume card. U7 Variable reward inside play only (Wild Round ~1 in 6 with printed odds; combos; speed bonus). U8 Reciprocity: daily grant and floor before any ad; 'now-that' framing. U9 Social proof that is true: real counts, labelled bots, club totals. U10 Commitment devices the player sets (stake choice, 'I support X', rival list) - Cialdini Consistency used for self-authored commitments only. U11 Bracketed/friends/club/percentile boards with opt-out. U12 Ownership (Octalysis CD4): Vault, Supporter Card, earned cosmetics - no second currency. U13 Ceremonies and juice (Swink: response under ~100 ms; 'Juice it or lose it') as feedback, never as reward inflation. U14 Loss aversion as a tier FLOOR (you cannot fall below a reached tier this season) rather than as a threat. NEVER LIST (deceptive or enforcement-exposed): N1 fabricated near-miss; N2 fake countdowns/scarcity; N3 streak repair for coins or ads, alarmist streak pushes without shield; N4 unclosable/fake-close ads, ads inside a live round, ads before the result receipt; N5 confirmshaming decline buttons; N6 silent devaluation of coins or entitlements, hidden rule changes (timers, badge eligibility); N7 randomised paid/ad-gated rewards, hidden bot fills, undisclosed matchmaking; N8 auto-queued next duel, overlay chains, nagging; N9 fake opponents/presence/activity, unconsented nudges from profile views; N10 hidden costs at the stake/entry tap, currency bundles, a second currency; N11 child-directed exhortation, profiled ads to minors, allegiance targeting for unverified ages; N12 loss-streak difficulty rigging (economy.mjs header) and any 'mercy' that is not disclosed; N13 pre-selected opt-ins (notifications, marketing, data sharing) - FTC report 'Tricking Consumers into Sharing Data' (Vizio default settings), DSA Art 25(3) default settings; N14 forced account creation before first play. COMPETITOR COMPLAINT -> NEVER MAP: TC01 -> N4; TC02 -> N8; TC03 -> N4 + N6; SP01 -> N4; SP02 -> N4; SP03 -> N6; QP01 -> N4; QP02 (unidentifiable opponents) -> N9 (identity must be recognisable and honest); QP05 -> N7 (ad-bought advantage) and N10; QP06 -> N9; QD01 -> N7 (bot labelling); QD02 (repeats reward memorised taps) -> N6/N7 fairness (exposure-aware selection); QD04 -> N6; Duolingo L01-L04 (energy pressure) -> N3.

findings.finding: MARKET-SPECIFIC ENFORCEMENT NOTES FOR THE AD-COIN MODEL. USA: FTC Act s.5 deception/unfairness is the live authority; the Epic order (finalised March 2023 per compliance.json) bars charging via dark patterns and account lockouts over disputes - with no purchases the analogues are coin confiscation and account suspension flows, which must have a receipt and an appeal; COPPA applies to under-13 accounts (Epic paid a separate $275m COPPA penalty). EU: the CPC virtual-currency principles are soft law and expressly exclude non-purchasable currencies, so keeping coins non-purchasable is the single biggest de-risking decision; UCPD Annex I points 7, 20, 22, 28 are hard law; 'free' claims (point 20) mean 'free coins' copy must not hide an unavoidable cost - an ad is a cost of attention, so say 'earn coins by watching an ad', not 'free coins'; DSA Arts 25/28 bite only if the service is an 'online platform' - public leaderboards and clubs are the features that could tip it (compliance.json risks[37]); the Digital Fairness Act (proposal expected H2 2026, dark patterns + addictive design) will land on this category. INDIA: the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act 2025 (assent 22 Aug 2025; Rules notified 22 Apr 2026; in force 1 May 2026) criminalises 'online money games' - 'a user paying money or other stakes in expectation of receiving monetary or other enrichment' regardless of skill; an 'online social game' is 'offered solely for recreation, entertainment, or skill development' and may charge a subscription 'not in the nature of a stake or wager'. Coins earned by watching ads, staked against another player for more coins that cannot be cashed out, are not money and yield no monetary enrichment, but 'other stakes' / 'other enrichment' is untested - compliance.json marks purchased-coin staking UNSETTLED; ad-earned coin staking is likewise UNVERIFIED and needs counsel before India launch, with a policy-engine rule row that can disable staking (keep practice drills and unstaked duels) in IN without a deploy. Advertising rule: penalties for advertising money games (up to 2 years / Rs 50 lakh) mean no cross-promotion of any real-money app in the ad inventory served in India - add a blocklist at the ad seam. DPDP: under-18 = child; no targeted ads to children; verifiable parental consent; children's-obligation breach penalty up to Rs 200 crore. Dream11 paused all paid contests on 21 Aug 2025 (over 90% of its revenue), which means India's sports-fan apps have moved to free formats - a signal that the free, ad-funded sports format faces well-funded incumbents there (a competitor lane point, noted for the founder).

recommendations.what: Delete gems as a currency; run one non-purchasable coin economy and move all cosmetics to achievement/season unlocks. Remove the 'duel-entry' ad placement and restrict 'continue' to practice drills.
recommendations.why: Two-tier currencies and ad-gated match entry are the Cognosphere 'currency confusion' and 'forced action' patterns; a non-purchasable currency keeps the CPC virtual-currency principles off the product (footnote 2) and the India 'money game' question narrower.

recommendations.what: Ship the 'priced ad card': reward, duration, visible daily cap and the free alternatives (daily grant, floor timer, win) on one surface, shown only after the result receipt is saved and never inside a round.
recommendations.why: Google Play's rewarded-ad exemption requires explicit opt-in; SP01/SP02/QP01/TC03 show ads mid-play and black screens are the top churn complaints in the inspected reviews.

recommendations.what: Leaderboards: bracketed weekly leagues of 30 by sport tier, friends board as default, club and derby-week boards, percentile-only global view, neighbourhood window (+/-2), opt-out, no bots, and a DSA scoping review before public boards launch.
recommendations.why: Hanus & Fox 2015, Christy & Fox 2014 and Landers 2017 show absolute global boards demotivate and act as impossible goals; Duolingo's bracketed leagues raised learning time 17%; public user-authored handles may make the service a DSA online platform.

recommendations.what: Supporter Card profile with one allegiance per sport (club/franchise/team/driver+constructor), per-sport rating and ranks, rivals list; guest-first with in-place principal promotion; age band at sign-up driving contextual-only ads for under-18/unverified.
recommendations.why: BIRG (Cialdini 1976) makes allegiance the cheapest identity hook; DPDP, DSA Art 28(2) and COPPA 2025 all bar profiled ads to minors; forced account creation is an 18% abandonment reason in Baymard's survey.

recommendations.what: Align seasons and streaks to the real calendars already verified (PL 21 Aug 2026-30 May 2027; NBA 20 Oct 2026-11 Apr 2027; F1 14 Mar-12 Dec 2027; MLB 25 Mar-26 Sep 2027 + WS 22-30 Oct; CWC 4 Oct-21 Nov 2027; IPL window TBC) with matchweek/race-weekend streaks, free shields, and an off-season 'Hot Stove/Transfer Window' mode; build an MLB lockout fallback because the CBA expires 1 Dec 2026.
recommendations.why: Real fixtures are honest urgency (UCPD Annex I point 7 bans false time limits) and the strongest daily external trigger available; weekly granularity lowers streak anxiety.

recommendations.what: Adopt the NEVER list as a release gate in the gamification-advisor skill (criterion 5 'Honesty') and add the complaint-to-pattern map as regression checks: no ad before receipt, no fake close, neutral decline copy, no pre-selected opt-ins, no silent coin-rule changes, bots labelled on every board.
recommendations.why: Each NEVER item maps to a live FTC/CPC/DSA precedent or to a named competitor complaint in the repo's review corpus.

recommendations.what: Get counsel's written view on (a) ad-earned coin staking under India's Act s.2(1)(g) 'other stakes/other enrichment', (b) use of league/club/driver names in ranks and share cards, and (c) an ad-inventory blocklist for real-money gaming ads in India; wire a policy-engine rule row that disables staking per region without a deploy.
recommendations.why: The Act is criminal, extraterritorial and untested on non-cashable coins; advertising money games carries up to 2 years / Rs 50 lakh.

recommendations.what: Instrument the loop before tuning it: D1/D7/D30 of duel-completers as the One Metric That Matters, with ad opt-in rate, ads per DAU, cap-hit rate, streak-shield usage, board opt-out rate and K-factor as guardrails; treat the 20 ads/day cap and region coin values as hypotheses.
recommendations.why: No primary rewarded-ad benchmark could be verified this session; Lean Analytics and Traction both say measure the loop before scaling a channel.

recommendations.what: Virality pack: 'Settle it' challenge links, sport-coded result share cards with percentile, derby-week club totals, coin-for-coin referral with cap and neutral copy, invite-a-rival from the rivals list.
recommendations.why: Berger's STEPPS (Social Currency, Public, Emotion) and Cialdini's Unity are the honest drivers; referral reward is coins only, so no prize/consideration issue.

recommendations.what: Publish an in-app 'Rules of the coin' page (earn rates by region, caps, stakes, floor, what changes and when) and a change log; announce any economy change one matchweek ahead.
recommendations.why: TC03 and QD04 show devaluation without notice destroys trust; DCD Art 19 is the EU standard for modifying a digital service and is the right bar even without purchases.

recommendations.what: Later: per-sport Glicko rating, exposure-aware question selection (QD02), and a rival 'head-to-head' record on the Supporter Card.

risks: India: staking ad-earned coins may still be read as 'other stakes' in expectation of 'other enrichment' under s.2(1)(g) of the 2025 Act (criminal, extraterritorial, director liability); no ruling exists. Ship India with a region rule row that can switch staking off without a deploy, and get counsel's written view first.

EU DSA scope creep: public leaderboards, clubs and shareable cards with user-authored handles can flip the service from hosting service to 'online platform' (Arts 20-28 incl. Art 25 dark patterns and Art 28 minors). Gate every social feature through a DSA scoping review.

Minors: a sports trivia game will be deemed to reach under-18s (CPC position); DPDP bars targeted ads to under-18s, DSA Art 28(2) bars profiled ads to minors, COPPA 2025 requires separate consent for targeted-ad disclosures. Contextual-only rewarded ads for unverified ages will lower eCPM in India and the EU - model it.

Ad-provider failure modes (black screens, no fill, unverified completions) are the top complaint pattern in the inspected reviews; a web rewarded ad may lack server-side verification, so reward on receipt idempotency and never on client callbacks alone.
Trademark/IP: club, league, driver and team names in ranks, cosmetics and share cards are UNVERIFIED for clearance; use colours and generic names until cleared.

Streaks and leagues are the two mechanics with the strongest evidence of both retention gains and demotivation; without the shields, weekly resets, percentile views and opt-outs they become the NEVER list.
MLB CBA expiry 1 Dec 2026 may leave the baseball season without fixtures in spring 2027; IPL 2027 dates unknown; the events calendar is static and needs a monthly human refresh (events-calendar.md).

Region-differentiated coin rewards (US 50 vs IN 20 per ad) are defensible because coins have no money value, but must be printed in the rules page and never changed silently (TC03/QD04 pattern; DCD Art 19 standard).
The Digital Fairness Act (proposal expected H2 2026) may add addictive-design duties; anything on the NEVER list would need to be unbuilt, so do not build it.
Benchmarks for rewarded-ad economics are unverified; the coin config is a hypothesis and the business case should not cite opt-in or retention lifts until measured.
